question: (a) Write the relationship between resistivity and resistance of a cylindrical conductor of length l and area of cross-section A. Hence derive the SI unit of resistivity. (b) Why are alloys used in electrical heating devices ?
solution: (a) R = ρl/A, so ρ = RA/l. The SI unit of resistivity is Ω m. (b) Alloys generally have high resistivity and high melting points and can withstand high temperatures, making them suitable for heating elements.

subject: Science
question: (a) (i) Draw two isomeric structures of Butene (C4H8). (ii) Name the following compounds : (I) H–C–C–C–Cl with H atoms completing valency around each carbon. (II) H–C–C–C–C–H with a C=O group on the third carbon and H atoms completing valency. (iii) Write the chemical equations for the following reactions. Mention one essential condition each for these reactions to take place. (I) Ethanol undergoes complete oxidation (II) Propene undergoes hydrogenation (III) Ethanoic acid reacts with ethanol OR (b) (i) A carbon compound X is a good solvent. On reaction with sodium, X forms two products Y and Z. Z is used to convert vegetable oil into vegetable ghee. Identify and name X, Y and Z. Also write the equation of reaction of X with sodium to justify your answer. (ii) Write chemical equations to show what happens when ethanol : (I) burns in oxygen/air. (II) is heated at 443 K in excess conc. H2SO4. (III) reacts with acidified potassium dichromate.
solution: (a) (i) Examples: but-1-ene, CH2=CH–CH2–CH3 and but-2-ene, CH3–CH=CH–CH3. (ii) The structures shown are 1-chloropropane and butan-2-one. (iii) Ethanol + O2 → CO2 + H2O (complete combustion); propene + H2 → propane (Ni catalyst); ethanoic acid + ethanol ⇌ ethyl ethanoate + water (conc. H2SO4). OR (b) X is ethanol, Y is sodium ethoxide and Z is hydrogen; however, hydrogen is not the product used for hydrogenation in the stated wording—the industrial hydrogen used for converting vegetable oil to ghee is supplied separately. For the sodium reaction: 2C2H5OH + 2Na → 2C2H5ONa + H2. Ethanol burns to CO2 and H2O, gives ethene with conc. H2SO4 at 443 K, and is oxidised to ethanoic acid by acidified potassium dichromate.

subject: Science
concept: Human Female Reproductive System and Contraception
question: (a) (i) Write the functions of the following parts of human female reproductive system : (I) Ovary (II) Fallopian tube (III) Uterus (ii) State briefly two contraceptive methods used by human males. OR (b) (i) Differentiate between self-pollination and cross-pollination. (ii) Identify A, B and C in the diagram given below and write one function of each.
solution: (a) Ovary produces ova and female hormones; the fallopian tube carries the ovum and is the usual site of fertilisation; the uterus is the site of implantation and development of the embryo. Male contraceptive methods include condoms and vasectomy. OR (b) Self-pollination transfers pollen to the stigma of the same flower/plant, while cross-pollination transfers pollen to a flower on another plant of the same species. In the diagram, A is stigma, B is pollen tube and C is male gamete(s) entering the ovule; their functions are receiving pollen, carrying male gametes and participating in fertilisation.

subject: Science
question: (a) (i) The power of a lens ‘X’ is – 2·5 D. Name the lens and determine its focal length in cm. For which eye defect of vision will an optician prescribe this type of lens as a corrective lens ? (ii) “The value of magnification ‘m’ for a lens is – 2.” Using new Cartesian Sign Convention and considering that an object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of this lens, state : (I) the nature of the image formed; (II) size of the image compared to the size of the object; (III) position of the image, and (IV) sign of the height of the image. (iii) The numerical values of the focal lengths of two lenses A and B are 10 cm and 20 cm respectively. Which one of the two will show higher degree of convergence/divergence ? Give reason to justify your answer. OR (b) (i) Draw a ray diagram to show the refraction of a ray of light through a rectangular glass slab when it falls obliquely from air into glass. (ii) State Snell’s law of refraction of light. (iii) Differentiate between the virtual images formed by a convex lens and a concave lens on the basis of : (I) object distance, and (II) magnification.
solution: (a) (i) P = −2.5 D, so X is a concave lens and f = 1/P = −0.4 m = −40 cm; it corrects myopia. (ii) With m = −2 and u = −20 cm, v = mu = +40 cm. The image is real, inverted and twice the object size; image height is negative. (iii) The 10 cm focal-length lens has greater power and therefore greater convergence/divergence. OR (b) In a glass slab the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray with lateral displacement. Snell’s law: n1 sin i = n2 sin r. A convex lens forms a virtual, erect and magnified image when the object is within its focal length; a concave lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image.

subject: Science
concept: Brine Electrolysis and Water of Crystallisation
question: Seawater contains many salts dissolved in it. Common salt is separated from these salts. Deposits of solid salt are also found in several parts of the world. These large crystals are often brown due to impurities. This is called rock salt and is mined like coal. The common salt is an important raw material for chemicals of daily use. (a) Write balanced chemical equations to show the products formed during electrolysis of brine. (b) List two uses of any one product obtained during electrolysis of brine. (c) (i) A mild non-corrosive basic salt ‘A’, used for faster cooking, is strongly heated to produce a compound ‘B’, that is used for removing permanent hardness of water. Identify A and B and also write the equation for the reaction that occurs when A is heated. OR (c) (ii) Define water of crystallisation. Give two examples of salts that have water of crystallisation.
solution: (a) 2NaCl + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2 + Cl2. (b) Chlorine is used for water purification and manufacture of bleaching powder. (c)(i) A is sodium hydrogen carbonate (NaHCO3) and B is sodium carbonate (Na2CO3): 2NaHCO3 → Na2CO3 + CO2 + H2O. OR (c)(ii) Water of crystallisation is the fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a crystalline salt. Examples: CuSO4·5H2O and Na2CO3·10H2O.

subject: Science
question: The maintenance functions of all living organisms must go on even when they are not doing anything particular. Even when we are just sitting in a class or even asleep, this maintenance job has to go on. These maintenance processes require energy to prevent damage and break-down of cells and tissues, which is obtained by the individual organism from the food prepared by the autotrophs, called producers. (a) Name and define the process by which green plants prepare food. (b) Write chemical equation involved in the above process. (c) (i) State in proper sequence the events that occur in synthesis of food by desert plants. OR (c) (ii) Explain giving reasons what happens to the rate at which the green plants will prepare food (I) during cloudy weather, and (II) when stomata get blocked due to dust.
solution: (a) Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to synthesise food from carbon dioxide and water in the presence of chlorophyll. (b) 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2, in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll. (c)(i) Desert plants generally open stomata at night to take in CO2, store it as organic acids, and use the stored CO2 during daytime photosynthesis while stomata remain closed. OR (c)(ii) Photosynthesis decreases in cloudy weather because light intensity is lower, and decreases when stomata are blocked because CO2 cannot enter efficiently.

subject: Science
question: In our homes, we receive the supply of electric power through a main supply also called mains, either supported through overhead electric poles or by underground cables. In our country the potential difference between the two wires (live wire and neutral wire) of this supply is 220 V. (a) Write the colours of the insulation covers of the line wires through which supply comes to our homes. (b) What should be the current rating of the electric circuit (220 V) so that an electric iron of 1 kW power rating can be operated ? (c) (i) What is the function of the earth wire ? State the advantage of the earth wire in domestic electric appliances such as electric iron. OR (c) (ii) List two precautions to be taken to avoid electrical accidents. State how these precautions prevent possible damage to the circuit/appliance.
solution: (a) Live wire: red/brown; neutral wire: black/blue (the paper uses the standard school colour convention). (b) I = P/V = 1000/220 ≈ 4.55 A, so a 5 A or higher suitable circuit rating is required. (c)(i) The earth wire provides a low-resistance path for leakage current and protects the user from electric shock. OR (c)(ii) Do not handle electrical appliances with wet hands and use proper fuse/MCB protection; these precautions reduce shock and overcurrent/fire risks.

subject: Science
question: The warning sign shown in the given figure must invariably be displayed/pasted on the containers which contain hydroxide of : (A) Aluminium (B) Calcium (C) Sodium (D) Magnesium
solution: Sodium hydroxide is highly corrosive and requires a corrosive warning sign. Correct option: (C).

subject: Science
question: Aluminium powder is used in thermit welding because : (A) Its reaction with iron is highly exothermic. (B) When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten iron is obtained. (C) When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten aluminium oxide is obtained to join railway tracks. (D) Its melting point is low as compared to iron and a molten alloy of iron and aluminium is formed on heating which is used to join railway tracks.
solution: Aluminium reduces iron(III) oxide to molten iron, producing a large amount of heat. Correct option: (B).

subject: Science
concept: Reaction of Zinc with Sodium Hydroxide
question: A few pieces of granulated zinc are taken in a test tube and 2 mL of sodium hydroxide solution is added to it. When the contents are warmed, the product formed is : (A) Na2ZnO (B) NaZnO2 (C) Na2ZnO2 (D) NaZn(OH)2
solution: Zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide on warming to form sodium zincate. Correct option: (B), NaZnO2.

subject: Science
question: Two metals zinc and tin are dissolved separately in definite proportions in molten copper (the primary metal) to obtain two different alloys respectively known as : (A) Bronze and Brass (B) Brass and Solder (C) Brass and Bronze (D) Solder and Bronze
solution: Copper with zinc forms brass, while copper with tin forms bronze. Correct option: (C).

subject: Science
question: The correct balanced chemical equation showing exothermic reaction in which natural gas burns in air is : (A) CH4 + O2 → CO2 + 2H2O (B) CH4 + 2O2 → 2CO2 + 2H2O + Energy (C) CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O (D) CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O + Energy
solution: Methane burns completely in oxygen to form one CO2, two H2O molecules and releases energy. Correct option: (D).

subject: Science
question: The essential element used in the synthesis of proteins is : (A) Nitrogen (B) Phosphorus (C) Iron (D) Magnesium
solution: Nitrogen is an essential constituent of amino acids and proteins. Correct option: (A).

subject: Science
question: The number of chromosomes in a cell division is halved. This kind of cell division is observed in : (A) Only testis (B) Only ovary (C) Ovary and testis both (D) All cells of the body
solution: Meiosis occurs during formation of gametes in both ovaries and testes. Correct option: (C).

subject: Science
question: One-cell thick blood vessels are known as : (A) Alveoli (B) Capillaries (C) Arteries (D) Veins
solution: Capillaries are microscopic, one-cell-thick blood vessels that allow exchange of materials. Correct option: (B).

subject: Science
question: Which one of the following statements is not correct for the plants raised by vegetative propagation ? (A) Can bear flowers and fruits earlier than those produced from seeds. (B) Those plants that have lost the capacity to produce seeds can be grown. (C) As compared to the parent plant, vegetatively propagated plants show more variations. (D) All the plants produced in this way are genetically similar to the parent plant.
solution: Vegetative propagation produces genetically similar plants with very little variation. Correct option: (C).

subject: Science
question: Observe the given figures A and B. When chhui-mui (sensitive) plant is touched, its leaves fold. This is due to : (A) Hormonal effect (B) Thermal effect (C) Change in amount of water in cells (D) Electromagnetic effect
solution: Touch causes changes in water content and turgor pressure of cells, resulting in folding of leaves. Correct option: (C).

subject: Science
question: Four identical resistors of 12 Ω each are connected in series to form a square ABCD as shown in the figure. The resistance of the network between the two points 1 and 2 is : (A) 48 Ω (B) 36 Ω (C) 9 Ω (D) 6 Ω
solution: The two paths between the opposite points each have two 12 Ω resistors in series, giving 24 Ω each. These two 24 Ω combinations are parallel, so equivalent resistance is 12 Ω. The answer depends on the exact positions of points 1 and 2 in the supplied figure.

subject: Science
question: If the absolute refractive indices of two media X and Y are 6/5 and 4/3 respectively, then the refractive index of Y with respect to X will be : (A) 10/9 (B) 9/10 (C) 9/8 (D) 8/9
solution: Refractive index of Y with respect to X = nY/nX = (4/3)/(6/5) = 10/9. Correct option: (A).

subject: Science
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question: In the human eye, most of the refraction for the light rays entering the eye occurs at the surface of : (A) Cornea (B) Crystalline lens (C) Pupil (D) Aqueous humor
solution: Most refraction of entering light occurs at the outer surface of the cornea. Correct option: (A).

subject: Science
question: The resistivity of a wire made of an alloy is generally : (A) Lower than that of its constituent metals. (B) Higher than that of its constituent metals. (C) Decreases with increase in its area of cross-section. (D) Increases with increase in its length.
solution: Alloys generally have higher resistivity than their constituent pure metals. Correct option: (B).

subject: Science
question: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the pole of a concave mirror. If its real and inverted image is formed at 60 cm in front of the mirror, the focal length of the mirror is : (A) –15 cm (B) –20 cm (C) +20 cm (D) +15 cm
solution: Using 1/f = 1/v − 1/u with u = −30 cm and v = −60 cm gives f = −20 cm. Correct option: (B).

subject: Science
question: Identify from the following a group containing all non-biodegradable substances. (A) Leather, Glass, Plastic (B) Cotton, Wood, Nylon (C) DDT, Polyester, Glass (D) Leather, Silk, Wool
solution: DDT, polyester and glass are non-biodegradable. Correct option: (C).

subject: Science
question: Assertion (A): Propanal and propanone are structural isomers. Reason (R): Propanal and propanone both have the same molecular formula.
solution: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the same molecular formula with different structures establishes structural isomerism. Correct option: (A).

subject: Science
question: Assertion (A): Nichrome is an alloy which is commonly used in electrical heating devices such as electric irons, toasters, etc. Reason (R): The resistivity of nichrome is high and its resistance decreases with increase in temperature.
solution: The Assertion is true, but the Reason is false because resistance of nichrome generally increases with temperature. Correct option: (C).

subject: Science
question: Assertion (A): A mango seed will germinate to form a mango tree. Reason (R): Heredity determines the process by which traits and characteristics are reliably inherited from parents to offspring.
solution: Both statements are true and the Reason explains why inherited characteristics determine the type of organism produced. Correct option: (A).

subject: Science
question: Assertion (A): Animals will not get energy if they eat (consume) coal as food. Reason (R): Specific enzymes are needed for the breakdown of a particular food.
solution: Both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains why coal cannot be digested to provide usable energy. Correct option: (A).

subject: Science
question: Balance the following chemical equations: (a) CO2 + H2O → C6H12O6 + O2 + H2O (b) Pb(NO3)2 → PbO + NO2 + O2

subject: Science
question: (a) Select from the following the members of same homologous series: (1) [structure shown in PDF] (2) [structure shown in PDF] (3) [structure shown in PDF] (4) [structure shown in PDF] (b) What happens to (i) the melting point, and (ii) the solubility of compounds as the molecular mass of the compounds in a homologous series increases?
solution: Members of the same homologous series have the same functional group and differ by –CH2– units. As molecular mass increases, melting point generally increases, while solubility in water generally decreases.

subject: Science
question: Study the given diagram and write the type of movement exhibited by: (a) Root, and (b) Shoot, mentioning the stimulus in each case.
solution: The root shows positive geotropism/gravitropism in response to gravity, while the shoot shows negative geotropism/gravitropism by growing away from gravity.

subject: Science
question: (a) Write one function each of the following, in a seed: (i) Seed coat (ii) Cotyledon (iii) Radicle (iv) Plumule OR (b) Write the main steps to culture yeast in the laboratory.
solution: (a) Seed coat protects the seed; cotyledon stores/provides food; radicle develops into the root; plumule develops into the shoot. OR (b) Prepare a nutrient medium, add yeast, maintain suitable warm conditions and allow the yeast to grow and multiply.

subject: Science
question: (a) Out of the two lenses, one concave and the other convex, state which one will diverge a parallel beam of light falling on it. Draw a ray diagram to show the principal focus of the lens. OR (b) A ray of light after refraction from a convex lens emerges parallel to its principal axis. (i) Draw a labelled ray diagram to show it. (ii) In this case, the incident ray before refraction from the lens passes through a point on its principal axis. Name the point.
solution: (a) A concave lens diverges a parallel beam and its principal focus is virtual on the same side as the incident light. OR (b) The incident ray passes through the principal focus on the object side; after refraction it emerges parallel to the principal axis.

subject: Science
question: An electric fuse is rated 8 A. Can it be used with an electrical appliance of rating 5 kW, 200 V? Justify your answer.
solution: Current required I = P/V = 5000/200 = 25 A. Since 25 A is much greater than the fuse rating of 8 A, the 8 A fuse cannot be used.

subject: Science
question: (a) (i) Define the term decomposition reaction. Write one chemical equation each for decomposition reaction where energy is supplied in the form of heat, light or electricity. (ii) Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost is considered an exothermic reaction. Why? OR (b) Why are decomposition reactions called the opposite of combination reactions? Write one chemical equation each for these two types of reactions mentioning the name of the reactant(s) and the product(s) involved in the reactions.
solution: A decomposition reaction is one in which a single compound breaks into two or more simpler substances. Examples: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2 by heat; 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl2 by sunlight; 2H2O → 2H2 + O2 by electricity. Compost formation releases heat because microorganisms decompose organic matter and release energy.

subject: Science
question: Study the experimental set-up given in the figure and answer the following questions: (a) Identify these metals from the following which can be used as ‘metal sample’ in the given set-up: Aluminium, Copper, Iron, Lead, Silver. (b) Write balanced chemical equations for the reaction in each case.
solution: The metals that can react with dilute acid and liberate hydrogen are aluminium, iron and lead under suitable conditions. Copper and silver do not liberate hydrogen with dilute non-oxidising acids. Representative reactions are Fe + 2HCl → FeCl2 + H2 and 2Al + 6HCl → 2AlCl3 + 3H2.

subject: Science
question: (a) What is meant by reflex arc? Where are they formed in the human body? (b) Why have reflex arcs evolved in animals?
solution: A reflex arc is the neural pathway followed by nerve impulses during a reflex action. It is mainly formed through the spinal cord and associated sensory and motor neurons. Reflex arcs provide rapid, automatic responses that protect the body from harmful stimuli.

subject: Science
question: The lowest part of the ear called earlobe, is closely attached to the side of the head in some of us (Figure ‘X’), and not in others, called free earlobe (Figure ‘Y’). Attached and free earlobes are two variants found in human populations. The gene for free earlobe is dominant over attached earlobes. (a) A man with attached earlobes marries a woman having free earlobes. 50% of their children have free earlobes and 50% have attached earlobes. Explain the inheritance of this trait and write the trait combinations of the progeny. (b) Write the gene combinations of the father and the mother in the above case.
solution: Let F represent free earlobe and f represent attached earlobe. The attached father is ff. Since half the children are attached, the free-earlobe mother must be Ff. Cross: ff × Ff gives 50% Ff (free) and 50% ff (attached).

subject: Science
question: An object is placed at a distance of 20 cm from the optical centre of a concave lens and its image is formed on the same side of the lens as the object. If the distance of the image from optical centre of the lens is 10 cm, use lens formula to determine (i) focal length, and (ii) power of the lens in new Cartesian sign conventions.
solution: u = −20 cm and v = −10 cm. Using 1/f = 1/v − 1/u, f = −20 cm. Power P = 1/f(m) = 1/(−0.20) = −5 D.

subject: Science
question: Resistance of a wire of length 1 m is 35 Ω at 20°C. If the diameter of the wire is 0.2 mm, determine the resistivity of the material of the wire at that temperature. How will the resistivity of the wire change if the length and diameter of the wire both are doubled? Justify your answer. (Given that π = 22/7)
solution: Radius = 0.1 mm = 1 × 10^-4 m. Area = πr² = 22/7 × 10^-8 m². Resistivity ρ = RA/l = 35 × (22/7 × 10^-8) ≈ 1.1 × 10^-6 Ω m. Resistivity is a property of the material at a given temperature, so doubling length and diameter does not change it.

subject: Science
question: Write the essential function performed by ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere. How is it formed in the upper atmosphere? Write the name of the group of chemicals mainly responsible for the depletion of ozone layer.
solution: The ozone layer absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun and protects living organisms. In the upper atmosphere, UV radiation splits O2 molecules into oxygen atoms, which combine with O2 to form O3. Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are major chemicals responsible for ozone depletion.

subject: Science
question: (a) (i) A compound ‘X’ having two carbon atoms in its molecule turns blue litmus red and 5–8% solution of ‘X’ in water is widely used as a preservative. Identify the compound ‘X’ and write its structure. (ii) Compare its pH nature with a mineral acid. (iii) ‘X’ on reacting with alcohols produces sweet smelling compounds, used in making perfumes. Name the reaction and write its chemical equation. (iv) When sodium carbonate is added to ‘X’, a colourless gas is produced which turns lime water milky. Write the chemical equation for the reaction giving the name of the salt produced. OR (b) (i) Differentiate between saturated and unsaturated hydrocarbons by giving one example each, with a structural formula. (ii) Write the method of converting an unsaturated hydrocarbon into a saturated hydrocarbon. Name the industry where this reaction is commonly used. (iii) Write the name and structure of a hydrocarbon having double bond and four carbon atoms in its one molecule.
solution: X is ethanoic acid, CH3COOH. It is a weak acid and has a higher pH than a strong mineral acid of comparable concentration. With ethanol it undergoes esterification: CH3COOH + C2H5OH ⇌ CH3COOC2H5 + H2O in presence of concentrated H2SO4. With sodium carbonate: 2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 → 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2; the salt is sodium ethanoate. In OR (b), saturated hydrocarbons contain only single bonds, while unsaturated hydrocarbons contain double or triple bonds. Unsaturated hydrocarbons are converted to saturated hydrocarbons by hydrogenation using H2/Ni, commonly used in the vegetable oil industry. A four-carbon hydrocarbon with a double bond is butene, e.g. CH2=CH–CH2–CH3.

subject: Science
concept: Magnetic Field and Fleming's Left Hand Rule
question: (a) The given figure shows the current passing through the straight conductor XY. (i) Copy the diagram and draw the magnetic field lines when current flows from conductor X to Y. (ii) Name and state the rule used in determining the direction of the magnetic field lines in the situation given above. (iii) State Fleming’s left hand rule. Using this rule, determine the direction of force applied on an electron entering a uniform magnetic field as shown in the figure. OR (b) (i) Define the term solenoid. Draw the pattern of the magnetic field lines in and around a current carrying straight solenoid. Mark on the pattern the (i) direction of current, (ii) direction of field lines near the ends of the solenoid, and (iii) region where the magnetic field is uniform. (ii) How would you make an electromagnet using a current carrying solenoid?
solution: For a straight current-carrying conductor, magnetic field lines are concentric circles around the conductor and their direction is determined by the right-hand thumb rule. Fleming's left-hand rule states that if the thumb, forefinger and middle finger of the left hand are mutually perpendicular, the forefinger gives magnetic-field direction, middle finger current direction and thumb force direction. For an electron, conventional current is opposite to its motion, so the force direction is determined accordingly. A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated wire; its field resembles that of a bar magnet and is nearly uniform inside. An electromagnet is made by placing a soft iron core inside a current-carrying solenoid.

subject: Science
question: (a) “The length of the small intestine in various animals depends on the food they eat.” Justify the statement. (ii) Discuss the role of the pancreas and bile juice in the digestion of food in human beings. (iii) How is the small intestine designed to absorb digested food? OR (b) (i) State the role of rings of cartilage present in the throat. (ii) Discuss the role of the ribs and diaphragm when air is taken in during the breathing cycle. (iii) Why do we get muscle cramps during heavy exercise? Explain.
solution: Herbivores generally have a longer small intestine because plant food contains cellulose and requires more time for digestion, whereas meat is easier to digest. Pancreatic juice contains enzymes for carbohydrates, proteins and fats; bile emulsifies fats and helps provide an alkaline medium. The small intestine has numerous villi that increase surface area and contain blood capillaries for absorption. Cartilage rings keep air passages open. During inhalation, ribs move upward and outward and the diaphragm contracts and flattens, increasing chest volume. During heavy exercise, oxygen may become insufficient and muscles undergo anaerobic respiration, producing lactic acid that can cause cramps.

subject: Science
question: Acid-base indicators can be used to distinguish between an acid and a base. Universal indicator, a mixture of several indicators, shows different colours at different concentrations of acids and bases, thereby indicating their pH on the pH scale of 0–14. The pH of a solution is measured by pH paper, which is a paper impregnated with a universal indicator. Answer the following questions: (a) Solution P is a strong acid while solution Q is a strong base. On the pH scale, where would you place the solutions P and Q? (b) A solution has a pH of 7. Name a compound you would use to (i) increase its pH, and (ii) decrease its pH. (c) (i) When the pH of a solution is decreased from 4 to 2, what effect does it produce on its hydronium ion concentration? State the colour change shown by the pH paper. OR (c) (ii) A person is feeling pain and irritation in the stomach due to indigestion. What could be the pH of the fluid in the stomach? Write the common name of the medicines people use for remedy. Give the chemical name of ‘milk of magnesia’ often used for this purpose.
solution: A strong acid has a pH near 0 and a strong base has a pH near 14. For a neutral solution at pH 7, adding a base such as sodium hydroxide increases pH, while adding an acid such as hydrochloric acid decreases it. Decreasing pH from 4 to 2 increases hydronium ion concentration by 100 times and the universal indicator changes from a higher-pH colour toward red. In indigestion, stomach fluid is strongly acidic; antacids are used for relief. Milk of magnesia is magnesium hydroxide, Mg(OH)2.

subject: Science
question: When a girl is born, the ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs. On reaching puberty, some of these start maturing. One matured egg is released every month by one of the ovaries. The two oviducts unite into an elastic bag-like structure known as uterus. (a) Write the site of fertilization in human female. (b) How does the uterus prepare itself to receive and nurture the growing embryo? Explain. (c) (i) What happens when the egg is not fertilized? OR (c) (ii) How does the developing embryo get nutrition from the mother’s blood? Explain.
solution: Fertilisation normally occurs in the fallopian tube/oviduct. The uterus develops a thick, blood-rich lining called the endometrium to receive and nourish the embryo. If fertilisation does not occur, the uterine lining breaks down and is shed as menstruation. The developing embryo receives nutrients and oxygen from the mother's blood through the placenta, while carbon dioxide and wastes pass back to the mother's blood.

subject: Science
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question: A person allowed a narrow beam of white light from the sun to enter a dark room through a small aperture and placed a glass prism in its path in such a manner that the beam falls on the face AB of the prism as shown in the figure. A screen S is placed on the other side of the prism, facing AC. On turning the prism slowly, a beautiful band of colours is obtained on the screen. It is the spectrum of sunlight. (a) Name the phenomenon due to which a prism splits the incident white light into a band of colours. (b) State the reason of getting a band of seven colours in the above case. (c) (i) Explain with the help of a labelled ray diagram, an experimental arrangement to show the recombination of the spectrum of white light. OR (c) (ii) Draw a labelled ray diagram to show the formation of a rainbow.
solution: The splitting of white light into its constituent colours by a prism is called dispersion of light. Seven colours are obtained because different colours have different wavelengths and hence undergo different deviations in glass. Recombination can be shown by passing the dispersed spectrum through a second inverted prism so that the colours combine to form white light. A rainbow is formed by dispersion, refraction and internal reflection of sunlight inside water droplets.

subject: Science
question: The most common method of extraction of metals from their oxide ores is:
solution: Reduction with carbon.

subject: Science
question: For p Al + q H₂O → r Al₂O₃ + s H₂, the values of p, q, r and s respectively are:

subject: Science
question: Given the structures of hydrocarbons, select the pair of structures which are related to each other.
solution: The correct pair is (i) and (iii).

subject: Science
question: Choose the incorrect statement about the common reaction used in hydrogenation of vegetable oils.
solution: The incorrect statement is that the addition reaction occurs in the presence of an acid catalyst. Hydrogenation uses a nickel or palladium catalyst.

subject: Science
question: Which option represents a family of salts?
solution: K₂SO₄, Na₂SO₄ and CaSO₄.

subject: Science
question: Select a pair of bisexual flowers from the following.
solution: Hibiscus and mustard.

subject: Science
question: The growth of pollen tubes towards ovules is an example of:
solution: Chemotropism.

subject: Science
question: Match the sites of fertilisation, implantation, sperm entry and removal of wastes from the developing embryo with the correct reproductive structures.
solution: The correct matching is a-(iii), b-(ii), c-(i), d-(iv).

subject: Science
question: The plant hormone present in greater concentration in areas of rapidly dividing cells is:
solution: Cytokinins.

subject: Science
question: Parasitic mode of nutrition is observed in:
solution: Cuscuta.

subject: Science
question: A candle flame is placed at a distance f from the pole of a convex mirror of focal length f. Where is its image formed?
solution: Behind the mirror at a distance f/2.

subject: Science
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question: Select the correct statement about scattering of light in the atmosphere.
solution: Fine particles in air scatter blue light more strongly than red light.

subject: Science
question: In domestic electric circuits, what are the usual colours of insulation for live, neutral and earth wires?
solution: Live wire: red; neutral wire: black; earth wire: green.

subject: Science
question: The strength of the magnetic field inside a long current-carrying solenoid does not depend upon:
solution: The radius of the coil.

subject: Science
question: Which statement is not true about a bar magnet?
solution: The direction of magnetic field lines inside a bar magnet is from its north pole to its south pole. Inside the magnet, the direction is from south to north.

subject: Science
question: Other than abiotic components, which biotic components are not required to make an aquarium with small herbivorous fishes a self-sustaining system?
solution: Terrestrial plants and terrestrial animals, i.e. (ii) and (iii) according to the paper's options?

subject: Science
question: Assertion: Brass is prepared by first melting copper and then dissolving tin into it in a definite proportion. Reason: The primary metal of brass is copper.
solution: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

subject: Science
question: Assertion: Use of jute bags for shopping reduces pollution. Reason: Jute is biodegradable and its bags can be reused as needed.
solution: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

subject: Science
question: Assertion: During writing or talking, the nervous system sends messages to muscles. Reason: Cranial nerves and spinal nerves form the peripheral nervous system.
solution: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

subject: Science
question: Assertion: Magnetic field lines around a bar magnet never intersect. Reason: The magnetic field is a quantity having both magnitude and direction.
solution: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but the Reason is not the correct explanation of why field lines do not intersect.

subject: Science
question: List the possible sources of energy required in decomposition reactions and illustrate any one with an example.
solution: Energy may be supplied as heat, light or electricity. For example, calcium carbonate decomposes on heating: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂.

subject: Science
question: A compound X is used to bleach washed clothes and to disinfect drinking water. Identify X, state its representation and describe its preparation with an equation.
solution: X is bleaching powder, CaOCl₂. It is prepared by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime: Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ → CaOCl₂ + H₂O.

subject: Science
question: State the main function of veins in the human circulatory system. Why do they not need thick walls?
solution: Veins carry blood towards the heart. They do not need thick muscular walls because blood flows through them at relatively low pressure.

subject: Science
question: Justify the statement that the sex of children is determined by the type of sex chromosome inherited from the father.
solution: The mother contributes only an X chromosome, whereas the father contributes either X or Y. XX gives a female child and XY gives a male child.

subject: Science
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question: A student cannot read textbooks clearly but can read the blackboard from the last row. Name the defect, give two causes and state the lens needed for correction.
solution: The defect is hypermetropia. It may be caused by a short eyeball or insufficient converging power of the eye lens. It is corrected with a convex lens.

subject: Science
question: Four resistors of 2 Ω each form a square ABCD. Determine the equivalent resistance between A and B.
solution: Between A and B, one 2 Ω resistor is directly connected and the other two 2 Ω resistors form a series path of 4 Ω. Thus equivalent resistance = (2 × 4)/(2 + 4) = 4/3 Ω.

subject: Science
question: What change is observed when copper powder is heated? Name the phenomenon, write the balanced equation and distinguish it from the coating formed on copper articles exposed to air.
solution: Copper powder turns black because it is oxidised to copper(II) oxide: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO. The black CuO formed on heating is a direct oxidation product. Copper articles exposed to moist air gradually develop a green coating of basic copper carbonate, CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂.

subject: Science
question: Briefly describe the preparation of sodium hydroxide and sodium hydrogen carbonate from common salt and write the balanced equations. OR: Design an experiment to demonstrate that alcohol and glucose contain hydrogen but are not acids, and give the reason.
solution: Brine is electrolysed to produce sodium hydroxide: 2NaCl + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + Cl₂ + H₂. Carbon dioxide is passed through brine/ammoniated brine to obtain sodium hydrogen carbonate: NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃. OR: Alcohol and glucose contain hydrogen but do not ionise to produce H⁺ ions in aqueous solution, so they are not classified as acids.

subject: Science
question: Why is blood circulation in vertebrates called double circulation? Trace its path in a flow chart.
solution: Blood passes through the heart twice in one complete cycle: once through pulmonary circulation and once through systemic circulation. Path: body → vena cava → right atrium → right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary vein → left atrium → left ventricle → aorta → body.

subject: Science
question: A pure round yellow pea plant is crossed with a pure wrinkled green plant. State the appearance of F₁, possible F₂ trait combinations and their ratio, and explain the new combinations.
solution: F₁ seeds are all round and yellow. F₂ shows round yellow, round green, wrinkled yellow and wrinkled green in the ratio 9:3:3:1. New combinations arise due to independent assortment of alleles during gamete formation.

subject: Science
chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
question: A person's far point is much nearer than infinity. Name the defect, give two causes, state the corrective lens and explain its function.
solution: The defect is myopia. It may result from an elongated eyeball or excessive converging power of the eye lens. It is corrected with a concave lens, which diverges incoming light so that the eye lens forms the image on the retina.

subject: Science
question: Name and state the rule determining the force on a current-carrying conductor in a uniform magnetic field. Also identify when the force on a positive charge is maximum and minimum.
solution: Fleming's left-hand rule determines the force direction. The force is maximum when the velocity/current is perpendicular to the magnetic field and minimum (zero) when it is parallel to the field.

subject: Science
question: Explain why energy flow in a food chain is unidirectional. If 10,000 J is available at the producer level, how much reaches secondary consumers?
solution: Energy flows from the Sun to producers and then to consumers and is not returned to the previous trophic level. Only about 10% passes to the next level. Thus 10,000 J → 1,000 J at primary consumers → 100 J at secondary consumers.

subject: Science
question: From K, Ca, Al, Cu, Ag and Fe, identify metals fitting the stated oxygen-reaction conditions. Explain amphoteric oxides with aluminium oxide and define alkalis.
solution: I: Ag; II: Al; III: K; IV: Cu. Amphoteric oxides react with both acids and bases. Aluminium oxide is amphoteric: Al₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O and Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO₂ + H₂O. Alkalis are bases soluble in water, e.g. NaOH.

subject: Science
question: Describe the extraction of mercury from cinnabar and copper from a sulphide ore, and name the compounds formed as coatings on silver and copper articles exposed to air. OR: Describe the extraction of mercury from cinnabar and copper from sulphide ore, and name the coatings formed on silver and copper articles exposed to air.
solution: Cinnabar is heated in air: 2HgS + 3O₂ → 2HgO + 2SO₂, followed by reduction: 2HgO → 2Hg + O₂. Copper sulphide is roasted and then reduced to obtain copper. Silver forms a black coating of Ag₂S, while copper forms a green coating of basic copper carbonate, CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂. OR: Mercury is obtained from cinnabar by roasting and subsequent reduction of HgO; copper is extracted from sulphide ore by roasting/reduction. Silver forms Ag₂S coating and copper forms basic copper carbonate, CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂.

subject: Science
question: Identify the shown reproductive structures, identify the unicellular organism, state two advantages of asexual reproduction and explain one method of asexual reproduction in Hydra.
solution: The figure represents an asexual mode of reproduction and includes a unicellular organism. Asexual reproduction is faster and requires only one parent, producing genetically similar offspring. Hydra reproduces by budding: a small bud develops on the parent by repeated cell division and eventually detaches as an independent organism.

subject: Science
question: From V-I graphs identify the series and parallel combinations of R₁ and R₂. Also arrange three 10 Ω resistors to obtain 15 Ω, or calculate the current in a 6 V circuit containing five series resistors of 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 0.5 Ω.
solution: For a V-I graph, the series combination has the greater resistance (greater slope), while the parallel combination has the lower resistance. Three 10 Ω resistors can give 15 Ω by connecting two in parallel (5 Ω) and the third in series: 5 + 10 = 15 Ω. In the alternative, total resistance is 1.5 Ω, so current = 6/1.5 = 4 A.

subject: Science
question: Two salts A and B are used for washing, with salt A also used for bathing. Four test tubes contain rain/tubewell water with A/B. Identify the test tube with minimum foam, distinguish A and B, and explain ester reaction with alkali or hardness of water.
solution: Tubewell water with the soap-like salt A gives the minimum foam if it contains hardness-producing ions. Salt A is soap and salt B is detergent. Esters react with sodium hydroxide to form alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid (saponification): RCOOR′ + NaOH → RCOONa + R′OH. Hard water contains Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺ ions, which react with soap to form insoluble scum.

subject: Science
question: A person becomes frightened while climbing a rocky hill. Name the hormone or its source gland, state two body responses and distinguish hormonal chemical signals from nerve impulses.
solution: The hormone is adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal glands. It increases heart rate and breathing rate and redirects more blood towards skeletal muscles. Hormonal signals are chemical messages carried through the blood and generally act more slowly and for longer, whereas nerve impulses are electrical signals transmitted rapidly through neurons.

subject: Mathematics
question: If the sum of zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = 2x² − k√2x + 1 is √2, then the value of k is:
solution:
For ax² + bx + c, sum of zeroes = −b/a.

Here, a = 2 and b = −k√2.

So,
−(−k√2)/2 = √2
k√2/2 = √2
k = 2

Answer: 2.

subject: Mathematics
question: If the probability of a player winning a game is 0.79, then the probability of his losing the same game is:
solution:
Probability of losing = 1 − Probability of winning
= 1 − 0.79
= 0.21

Answer: 0.21.

subject: Mathematics
question: If the roots of the equation ax² + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0 are real and equal, then which of the following relation is true?
solution:
For equal roots, the discriminant is zero.

b² − 4ac = 0
b² = 4ac

Therefore,
ac = b²/4.

Answer: ac = b²/4.

subject: Mathematics
question: In an A.P., if the first term a = 7, nth term an = 84 and the sum of first n terms Sn = 2093/2, then n is equal to:

subject: Mathematics
question: If two positive integers p and q can be expressed as p = 18a²b⁴ and q = 20a³b², where a and b are prime numbers, then LCM(p, q) is:
solution:
LCM of numerical parts: LCM(18, 20) = 180.

For a, take the highest power: a³.
For b, take the highest power: b⁴.

Therefore,
LCM(p, q) = 180a³b⁴.

subject: Mathematics
question: AD is a median of ΔABC with vertices A(5, −6), B(6, 4) and C(0, 0). Length AD is equal to:
solution:
Midpoint of BC:
D = ((6 + 0)/2, (4 + 0)/2)
D = (3, 2)

Using distance formula:
AD = √[(3 − 5)² + (2 + 6)²]
= √[4 + 64]
= √68

Answer: √68 units.

subject: Mathematics
question: If sec θ − tan θ = m, then the value of sec θ + tan θ is:
solution:
We know:
(sec θ − tan θ)(sec θ + tan θ) = sec²θ − tan²θ
= 1

Given sec θ − tan θ = m.

Therefore,
m(sec θ + tan θ) = 1

sec θ + tan θ = 1/m.

subject: Mathematics
question: From the data 1, 4, 7, 9, 16, 21, 25, if all the even numbers are removed, then the probability of getting at random a prime number from the remaining is:
solution:
After removing even numbers, remaining numbers are:
1, 7, 9, 21, 25

There are 5 numbers.
Only 7 is prime.

Probability = 1/5.

Answer: 1/5.

subject: Mathematics
question: For some data x₁, x₂, ..... xₙ with respective frequencies f₁, f₂, ..... fₙ, the value of Σfᵢ(xᵢ − x̄) is equal to:
solution:
By the definition of mean,
Σfᵢxᵢ = x̄Σfᵢ.

Therefore,
Σfᵢ(xᵢ − x̄)
= Σfᵢxᵢ − x̄Σfᵢ
= 0.

Answer: 0.

subject: Mathematics
question: The zeroes of a polynomial x² + px + q are twice the zeroes of the polynomial 4x² − 5x − 6. The value of p is:
solution:
For 4x² − 5x − 6, sum of zeroes = −b/a = 5/4.

The new zeroes are twice the original zeroes.
So their sum = 2 × 5/4 = 5/2.

For x² + px + q, sum of zeroes = −p.

Therefore,
−p = 5/2
p = −5/2.

subject: Mathematics
question: If the distance between the points (3, −5) and (x, −5) is 15 units, then the values of x are:
solution:
Using distance formula:
15 = √[(x − 3)² + (−5 + 5)²]
15 = √[(x − 3)²]

So,
|x − 3| = 15

x − 3 = 15 or x − 3 = −15

Therefore,
x = 18 or x = −12.

subject: Mathematics
question: If cos(α + β) = 0, then the value of cos((α + β)/2) is:
solution:
Since cos(α + β) = 0,
α + β = 90° (for the given principal value).

Therefore,
(α + β)/2 = 45°

cos 45° = 1/√2.

Answer: 1/√2.

subject: Mathematics
question: A solid sphere is cut into two hemispheres. The ratio of the surface area of sphere to that of two hemispheres taken together is:
solution:
Surface area of sphere = 4πr².

Surface area of two hemispheres together includes:
2 curved surface areas + 2 circular bases
= 4πr² + 2πr²
= 6πr².

Ratio = 4πr² : 6πr²
= 2 : 3.

subject: Mathematics
question: The middle observation of every data arranged in order is called:
solution:
The middle observation of an ordered data set is called the median.

Answer: Median.

subject: Mathematics
question: The volume of the largest right circular cone that can be carved out from a solid cube of edge 2 cm is:
solution:
For the largest cone, the base is a circle inscribed in one face of the cube.

Radius r = 2/2 = 1 cm
Height h = 2 cm

Volume of cone = 1/3 πr²h
= 1/3 × π × 1² × 2
= 2π/3 cm³.

subject: Mathematics
question: Two dice are rolled together. The probability of getting sum of numbers on the two dice as 2, 3 or 5, is:
solution:
Total outcomes = 6 × 6 = 36.

Sum 2: 1 outcome.
Sum 3: 2 outcomes.
Sum 5: 4 outcomes.

Favourable outcomes = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7.

Probability = 7/36.

subject: Mathematics
question: The centre of a circle is at (2, 0). If one end of a diameter is at (6, 0), then the other end is at:
solution:
The centre is the midpoint of the diameter.

Let the other endpoint be (x, 0).

2 = (6 + x)/2
4 = 6 + x
x = −2

Therefore, the other endpoint is (−2, 0).

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
question: In the given figure, graphs of two linear equations are shown. The pair of these linear equations is:
solution:
The two lines are distinct and parallel, so they never intersect.

Therefore, the pair has no solution and is inconsistent.

Answer: Inconsistent.

subject: Mathematics
question: Assertion: The tangents drawn at the end points of a diameter of a circle are parallel. Reason: Diameter of a circle is the longest chord.
solution:
The Assertion is true because both tangents are perpendicular to the same diameter and are therefore parallel.

The Reason is also true, but it does not explain why the tangents are parallel.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation.

subject: Mathematics
question: Assertion: If the graph of a polynomial touches x-axis at only one point, then the polynomial cannot be a quadratic polynomial. Reason: A polynomial of degree n (n > 1) can have at most n zeroes.
solution:
A quadratic polynomial can touch the x-axis at exactly one point when it has equal roots.

Therefore, the Assertion is false.

A polynomial of degree n can have at most n zeroes, so the Reason is true.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

subject: Mathematics
question: In a pack of 52 playing cards one card is lost. From the remaining cards, a card is drawn at random. Find the probability that the drawn card is queen of heart, if the lost card is a black card.
solution:
Total cards originally = 52.

The lost card is black, while the queen of hearts is a red card. Therefore, queen of hearts is definitely among the remaining cards.

Remaining cards = 52 − 1 = 51.

Favourable outcomes = 1.

Probability = 1/51.

Answer: 1/51.

subject: Mathematics
question: Evaluate: 2√2 cos 45° sin 30° + 2√3 cos 30°.

subject: Mathematics
question: If A = 60° and B = 30°, verify that sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B.
solution:
LHS:
sin(A + B) = sin(60° + 30°)
= sin 90°
= 1.

RHS:
sin60° cos30° + cos60° sin30°
= (√3/2)(√3/2) + (1/2)(1/2)
= 3/4 + 1/4
= 1.

Since LHS = RHS,
the identity is verified.

subject: Mathematics
question: In the given figure, ABCD is a quadrilateral. Diagonal BD bisects ∠B and ∠D both. Prove that (i) ΔABD ~ ΔCBD (ii) AB = BC.
solution:
(i) Since BD bisects ∠B,
∠ABD = ∠DBC.

Since BD also bisects ∠D,
∠ADB = ∠CDB.

Therefore, by AA similarity,
ΔABD ~ ΔCBD.

(ii) From similar triangles,
AB/BC = BD/BD = 1.

Therefore,
AB = BC.

subject: Mathematics
question: Prove that 5 − 2√3 is an irrational number. It is given that √3 is an irrational number.
solution:
Assume that 5 − 2√3 is rational.

Let:
5 − 2√3 = r,
where r is rational.

Then:
2√3 = 5 − r
√3 = (5 − r)/2.

Since 5 and r are rational, (5 − r)/2 is rational.
Therefore √3 would be rational.

But √3 is given to be irrational.
This is a contradiction.

Hence, 5 − 2√3 is irrational.

subject: Mathematics
question: Show that the number 5×11×17 + 3×11 is a composite number.
solution:
Take 11 common:
5×11×17 + 3×11
= 11(5×17 + 3)
= 11(85 + 3)
= 11 × 88
= 968.

Since 968 has factors other than 1 and itself, it is a composite number.

subject: Mathematics
question: Find the ratio in which the point (8/5, y) divides the line segment joining the points (1, 2) and (2, 3). Also find the value of y.
solution:
Let the ratio be m:n.

Using section formula for x-coordinate:
8/5 = (2m + 1n)/(m+n)

8m + 8n = 10m + 5n
3n = 2m
m:n = 3:2.

Now use section formula for y-coordinate:
y = (3×3 + 2×2)/(3+2)
= (9 + 4)/5
= 13/5.

Answer:
Ratio = 3:2
and y = 13/5.

subject: Mathematics
question: ABCD is a rectangle formed by the points A(−1, −1), B(−1, 6), C(3, 6) and D(3, −1). P, Q, R and S are mid-points of sides AB, BC, CD and DA respectively. Show that diagonals of quadrilateral PQRS bisect each other.
solution:
Find the midpoints:
P = (−1, 5/2)
Q = (1, 6)
R = (3, 5/2)
S = (1, −1)

Midpoint of PR:
((−1+3)/2, (5/2+5/2)/2) = (1, 5/2)

Midpoint of QS:
((1+1)/2, (6−1)/2) = (1, 5/2)

Both diagonals PR and QS have the same midpoint.

Therefore, diagonals of quadrilateral PQRS bisect each other.

subject: Mathematics
question: In a teachers' workshop, the number of teachers teaching French, Hindi and English are 48, 80 and 144 respectively. Find the minimum number of rooms required if in each room the same number of teachers are seated and all of them are of the same subject.
solution:
To have the same maximum number of teachers in each room, find HCF of 48, 80 and 144.

HCF(48, 80, 144) = 16.

So each room can contain 16 teachers.

French rooms = 48/16 = 3
Hindi rooms = 80/16 = 5
English rooms = 144/16 = 9

Total rooms = 3 + 5 + 9
= 17.

Answer: 17 rooms.

subject: Mathematics
question: Prove that tanθ/(1 − cotθ) + cotθ/(1 − tanθ) = 1 + secθ cosecθ.
solution:
Let tanθ = t. Then cotθ = 1/t.

LHS = t/(1 − 1/t) + (1/t)/(1 − t)

= t²/(t − 1) + 1/[t(1 − t)]

= t²/(t − 1) − 1/[t(t − 1)]

= (t³ − 1)/[t(t − 1)]

= (t − 1)(t² + t + 1)/[t(t − 1)]

= t + 1 + 1/t

= 1 + tanθ + cotθ

Since tanθ + cotθ = secθ cosecθ,

LHS = 1 + secθ cosecθ = RHS.

Hence proved.

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
question: Three years ago, Rashmi was thrice as old as Nazma. Ten years later, Rashmi will be twice as old as Nazma. How old are Rashmi and Nazma now?
solution:
Let present age of Rashmi = x years.
Let present age of Nazma = y years.

Three years ago:
x − 3 = 3(y − 3)

x − 3 = 3y − 9
x = 3y − 6 ...(1)

Ten years later:
x + 10 = 2(y + 10)

x + 10 = 2y + 20
x = 2y + 10 ...(2)

Equating (1) and (2):
3y − 6 = 2y + 10
y = 16.

Substitute y = 16:
x = 2(16) + 10 = 42.

Answer:
Rashmi = 42 years
Nazma = 16 years.

subject: Mathematics
question: In the given figure, AB is a diameter of the circle with centre O. AQ, BP and PQ are tangents to the circle. Prove that ∠POQ = 90°.
solution:
Since AQ and PQ are tangents from Q,
QA = QP.

Also,
OA = OP (radii of the circle).

OA ⟂ AQ and OP ⟂ PQ because radius is perpendicular to tangent.

Therefore, right triangles ΔQAO and ΔQPO are congruent by RHS.

Hence,
∠AOQ = ∠QOP.

Since A, O and B lie on the same straight line,
∠AOQ + ∠QOP = 180°.

The two equal angles are therefore 90° each.

Hence,
∠POQ = 90°.

subject: Mathematics
question: A circle with centre O and radius 8 cm is inscribed in a quadrilateral ABCD. If AD is perpendicular to DC, BC = 30 cm and BS = 24 cm, find the length of DC.
solution:
Tangents from the same external point are equal.

From B:
BS = BR = 24 cm.

Given BC = 30 cm,
CR = BC − BR
= 30 − 24
= 6 cm.

From C:
CQ = CR = 6 cm.

Since AD ⟂ DC, the radii to the points of contact on AD and DC are perpendicular. Thus the angle between the two tangents from D is 90°.

For a circle of radius 8 cm, the tangent lengths from D to the two adjacent points of contact are equal to 8 cm.

Therefore,
DQ = 8 cm.

DC = DQ + QC
= 8 + 6
= 14 cm.

Answer: 14 cm.

subject: Mathematics
question: The difference between the outer and inner radii of a hollow right circular cylinder of length 14 cm is 1 cm. If the volume of the metal used in making the cylinder is 176 cm³, find the outer and inner radii.
solution:
Let inner radius = r cm.
Then outer radius = r + 1 cm.

Volume of metal:
πh[(r+1)² − r²] = 176

Using h = 14 cm and π = 22/7:
(22/7) × 14 × [(r+1)² − r²] = 176

44(2r + 1) = 176
2r + 1 = 4
2r = 3
r = 3/2 = 1.5 cm.

Outer radius = r + 1 = 2.5 cm.

Answer:
Inner radius = 1.5 cm
Outer radius = 2.5 cm.

subject: Mathematics
question: An arc of a circle of radius 21 cm subtends an angle of 60° at the centre. Find: (i) the length of the arc (ii) the area of the minor segment of the circle made by the corresponding chord.
solution:
Given:
r = 21 cm
θ = 60°

(i) Length of arc:
L = θ/360° × 2πr
= 60/360 × 2 × 22/7 × 21
= 22 cm.

(ii) Area of minor segment
= Area of sector − Area of triangle.

Area of sector:
= 60/360 × π × 21²
= 1/6 × 22/7 × 441
= 231 cm².

For the triangle, two sides are radii and included angle is 60°.
Therefore the triangle is equilateral with side 21 cm.

Area of triangle:
= (√3/4) × 21²
= 441√3/4 cm².

Area of minor segment:
= 231 − 441√3/4 cm².

Answer:
Arc length = 22 cm.
Minor segment area = 231 − 441√3/4 cm².

subject: Mathematics
concept: Sum and Product of AP Terms
question: The sum of first and eighth terms of an A.P. is 32 and their product is 60. Find the first term and common difference of the A.P. Hence, also find the sum of its first 20 terms.
solution:
Let first term = a and common difference = d.

Eighth term:
a₈ = a + 7d.

Given:
a + a₈ = 32
2a + 7d = 32 ...(1)

Also,
a(a + 7d) = 60.

Let a₈ = b.
Then:
a + b = 32
ab = 60.

Therefore a and b are roots of:
t² − 32t + 60 = 0

(t − 2)(t − 30) = 0.

So the two values are 2 and 30.

For the increasing A.P.:
a = 2,
a₈ = 30.

Therefore:
2 + 7d = 30
7d = 28
d = 4.

Now,
S₂₀ = 20/2 [2a + 19d]
= 10[4 + 76]
= 800.

Answer:
First term = 2
Common difference = 4
S₂₀ = 800.

subject: Mathematics
question: In an A.P. of 40 terms, the sum of first 9 terms is 153 and the sum of last 6 terms is 687. Determine the first term and common difference of the A.P. Also, find the sum of all the terms of the A.P.
solution:
Let first term = a and common difference = d.

Given:
S₉ = 153

Using Sₙ = n/2[2a + (n−1)d]:
153 = 9/2[2a + 8d]
34 = 2a + 8d
17 = a + 4d ...(1)

The last 6 terms are terms 35 to 40.
Their sum is:
S₄₀ − S₃₄ = 687.

Alternatively, average of the last 6 terms is:
(a₃₅ + a₄₀)/2.

a₃₅ = a + 34d
a₄₀ = a + 39d

So:
6/2[(a+34d)+(a+39d)] = 687
3(2a + 73d) = 687
2a + 73d = 229 ...(2)

From (1):
a = 17 − 4d.

Substitute in (2):
2(17 − 4d) + 73d = 229
34 − 8d + 73d = 229
65d = 195
d = 3.

Therefore:
a = 17 − 12 = 5.

Sum of all 40 terms:
S₄₀ = 40/2[2(5) + 39(3)]
= 20[10 + 117]
= 20 × 127
= 2540.

Answer:
First term = 5
Common difference = 3
Sum of all 40 terms = 2540.

subject: Mathematics
question: If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, then prove that the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.
solution:
Let in ΔABC, a line DE be drawn parallel to BC, meeting AB at D and AC at E.

Since DE ∥ BC,
∠ADE = ∠ABC
and
∠AED = ∠ACB.

Also,
∠A is common.

Therefore,
ΔADE ~ ΔABC by AA similarity.

Hence, corresponding sides are proportional:
AD/AB = AE/AC.

Now:
AB = AD + DB
AC = AE + EC.

So,
AD/(AD+DB) = AE/(AE+EC).

Cross multiplying:
AD(AE + EC) = AE(AD + DB)

AD·AE + AD·EC = AE·AD + AE·DB

AD·EC = AE·DB

Therefore,
AD/DB = AE/EC.

Hence proved that the two sides are divided in the same ratio.

subject: Mathematics
question: A pole 6 m high is fixed on top of a tower. The angle of elevation of the top of the pole observed from a point P on the ground is 60° and the angle of depression of the point P from the top of the tower is 45°. Find the height of the tower and the distance of point P from the foot of the tower. (Use √3 = 1.73)
solution:
Let height of tower = h m.
Let distance of P from foot of tower = x m.

Height of pole = 6 m.

Angle of depression of P from top of tower = 45°.
Therefore angle of elevation of top of tower from P = 45°.

So,
tan45° = h/x
1 = h/x
h = x ...(1)

Total height from P to top of pole = h + 6.

Angle of elevation of top of pole = 60°.

Therefore:
tan60° = (h + 6)/x
√3 = (h + 6)/x

Using h = x:
√3 = (x + 6)/x
√3x = x + 6
x(√3 − 1) = 6

Using √3 = 1.73:
x(0.73) = 6
x ≈ 8.22 m.

Therefore height of tower:
h ≈ 8.22 m.

Answer:
Height of tower ≈ 8.22 m
Distance of P from foot of tower ≈ 8.22 m.

subject: Mathematics
question: A rectangular floor area can be completely tiled with 200 square tiles. If the length of each tile is increased by 1 unit, it would take only 128 tiles to cover the floor. Assuming the original length of each tile is x units: (i) make a quadratic equation from the above information, (ii) write the corresponding quadratic equation in standard form, (iii) find the value of x by factorisation OR solve the quadratic equation for x using quadratic formula.
solution:
(i) Original area of floor = 200x².

New side of each tile = x + 1.
Number of new tiles = 128.

Therefore,
200x² = 128(x + 1)².

(ii) Expand:
200x² = 128(x² + 2x + 1)
200x² = 128x² + 256x + 128
72x² − 256x − 128 = 0

Dividing by 8:
9x² − 32x − 16 = 0.

This is the standard form.

(iii) Factorisation:
9x² − 32x − 16 = 0

= (9x + 4)(x − 4) = 0.

Therefore:
9x + 4 = 0  →  x = −4/9
or
x − 4 = 0  →  x = 4.

Since length cannot be negative,
x = 4 units.

Answer: Original side of each tile = 4 units.

subject: Mathematics
question: BINGO is a game of chance. The host has 75 balls numbered 1 through 75. Each player has a BINGO card with some numbers written on it. The given table shows the data of one such game where 48 balls were used: 0–15: 8, 15–30: 9, 30–45: 10, 45–60: 12, 60–75: 9. Based on this information: (i) Write the median class. (ii) When first ball was picked up, what was the probability of calling out an even number? (iii) Find median of the given data OR find mode of the given data.
solution:
(i) Total frequency N = 48.

N/2 = 24.

Cumulative frequencies:
0–15 → 8
15–30 → 17
30–45 → 27
45–60 → 39
60–75 → 48

The 24th observation lies in the class 30–45.

Median class = 30–45.

(ii) Numbers from 1 to 75 contain 37 even numbers.

Total possible numbers = 75.

Probability of an even number = 37/75.

(iii) Median:
Median = l + [(N/2 − cf)/f] × h

Here:
l = 30
N = 48
cf = 17
f = 10
h = 15

Median = 30 + [(24 − 17)/10] × 15
= 30 + 7/10 × 15
= 30 + 10.5
= 40.5.

Therefore median = 40.5.

OR

Mode:
Modal class = 45–60 because it has highest frequency 12.

Mode = l + [(f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h

= 45 + [(12 − 10)/(24 − 10 − 9)] × 15
= 45 + (2/5) × 15
= 45 + 6
= 51.

Therefore mode = 51.

subject: Mathematics
question: A backyard is in the shape of a triangle ABC with right angle at B. AB = 7 m and BC = 15 m. A circular pit was dug inside it such that it touches the walls AC, BC and AB at P, Q and R respectively such that AP = x m. Based on this information: (i) Find the length of AR in terms of x. (ii) Write the type of quadrilateral BQOR. (iii) Find PC in terms of x and hence find x OR find x and hence find the radius of the circle.
solution:
(i) Tangents drawn from the same external point are equal.

From point A:
AP = AR.

Given AP = x m.
Therefore:
AR = x m.

(ii) Since the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact:
OQ ⟂ BC and OR ⟂ AB.

Since AB ⟂ BC, we get OQ ∥ AB and OR ∥ BC.

Thus BQOR has four right angles.
Also, BQ = OR = r and BR = OQ = r.

Therefore BQOR is a square.

(iii) From tangent property at B:
BQ = BR = r.

Since AB = 7:
AB = AR + RB
7 = x + r
r = 7 − x.

Since BC = 15:
BC = BQ + QC
15 = r + PC
PC = 15 − r.

Substitute r = 7 − x:
PC = 15 − (7 − x)
PC = x + 8.

Now AC = AP + PC
= x + (x + 8)
= 2x + 8.

Since ∠B = 90°:
AC² = AB² + BC²
AC² = 7² + 15²
= 49 + 225
= 274.

Therefore:
(2x + 8)² = 274
2x + 8 = √274
2x = √274 − 8
x = (√274 − 8)/2.

Approximately:
x ≈ 4.28 m.

Radius:
r = 7 − x
= 7 − (√274 − 8)/2
= (22 − √274)/2
≈ 2.72 m.

Answer:
AR = x m
BQOR is a square
PC = x + 8 m
x ≈ 4.28 m
Radius ≈ 2.72 m.

subject: Mathematics
question: Which term of the A.P. −29, −26, −23, ..., 61 is 16?
solution: Here, a = −29 and d = 3. Using aₙ = a + (n − 1)d: 16 = −29 + (n − 1)3. Therefore, 45 = 3(n − 1), so n − 1 = 15 and n = 16. Correct answer: 16th term (B).

subject: Mathematics
question: In the given figure, PT is tangent to a circle with centre O. Chord PQ subtends an angle of 65° at the centre. The measure of ∠QPT is:
solution: In triangle OPQ, OP = OQ because both are radii. Hence ∠OPQ = ∠OQP = (180° − 65°)/2 = 57.5°. Since radius OP is perpendicular to tangent PT, ∠OPT = 90°. Therefore ∠QPT = 90° − 57.5° = 32.5°. Correct answer: 32.5° (D).

subject: Mathematics
question: Tangents PA and PB to the circle centred at O from point P are perpendicular to each other. If PA = 5 cm, then the length of AB is:
solution: Since PA and PB are tangents, PA = PB = 5 cm. Also, ∠APB = 90°. By symmetry, OP bisects ∠APB, so ∠APO = 45°. In right triangle OAP, OA = PA = 5 cm, giving OP = 5√2 cm. The chord AB is perpendicular to OP and its half-length is 5/√2 cm. Hence AB = 5√2 cm. Correct answer: 5√2 cm (B).

subject: Mathematics
concept: Similarity of Triangles in a Circle
question: AB and CD are two chords of a circle intersecting at P. Choose the correct statement.
solution: Since AB and CD intersect at P, ∠APD = ∠CPB (vertically opposite angles). Also, ∠DAP = ∠BCP because both subtend the same chord DC. Hence ΔADP ∼ ΔBCP. Correct answer: (C).

subject: Mathematics
concept: Effect of Change in Observations on Median
question: If the value of each observation in a data is increased by 2, then the median of the new data:
solution: When every observation is increased by 2, the median also increases by 2. Correct answer: (A).

subject: Mathematics
question: If α and β are zeroes of the polynomial 2x² − 9x + 5, then the value of α² + β² is:
solution: For 2x² − 9x + 5, α + β = 9/2 and αβ = 5/2. Therefore, α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = (9/2)² − 2(5/2) = 81/4 − 5 = 61/4. Correct answer: 61/4 (B).

subject: Mathematics
question: After an examination, a teacher wants to know the marks obtained by the maximum number of students in her class. She requires to calculate:
solution: The value occurring most frequently is called the mode. Therefore, the required measure is mode. Correct answer: (B).

subject: Mathematics
chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
question: The value of k for which the system 3x − y + 8 = 0 and 6x − ky + 16 = 0 has infinitely many solutions is:
solution: For infinitely many solutions, a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ = c₁/c₂. Here, 3/6 = 1/2 and 8/16 = 1/2. Therefore, (−1)/(−k) = 1/2, giving k = 2. Correct answer: 2 (B).

subject: Mathematics
question: Point P divides the line segment joining A(4, −5) and B(1, 2) in the ratio 5:2. The coordinates of P are:
solution: Using the section formula for AP:PB = 5:2: P = ((5×1 + 2×4)/7, (5×2 + 2×(−5))/7) = (13/7, 0). Correct answer: (13/7, 0) (D).

subject: Mathematics
question: A box contains cards numbered 6 to 55. A card is drawn at random. The probability that the drawn card has a number which is a perfect square is:
solution: There are 55 − 6 + 1 = 50 cards. Perfect squares between 6 and 55 are 9, 16, 25, 36 and 49, i.e. 5 cards. Probability = 5/50 = 1/10. Correct answer: 1/10 (C).

subject: Mathematics
question: If sin θ = cos θ, where 0° < θ < 90°, then the value of sec θ · sin θ is:
solution: sec θ · sin θ = sin θ/cos θ = tan θ. Since sin θ = cos θ, tan θ = 1. Correct answer: 1 (C).

subject: Mathematics
question: Two dice are rolled together. The probability of getting the sum of the two numbers to be more than 10 is:
solution: Sum greater than 10 means 11 or 12. Possible outcomes are (5,6), (6,5), and (6,6): 3 favourable outcomes. Total outcomes = 36. Probability = 3/36 = 1/12. Correct answer: 1/12 (D).

subject: Mathematics
question: The value of k for which x = 2 is a solution of 5x² − 4x + (2 + k) = 0 is:
solution: Substitute x = 2: 5(2)² − 4(2) + 2 + k = 0. Therefore, 20 − 8 + 2 + k = 0, so 14 + k = 0 and k = −14. Correct answer: −14 (D).

subject: Mathematics
question: The perimeters of two similar triangles ABC and PQR are 56 cm and 48 cm respectively. PQ/AB is equal to:
solution: For similar triangles, the ratio of corresponding sides equals the ratio of their perimeters. Therefore, PQ/AB = 48/56 = 6/7. Correct answer: 6/7 (B).
