Print and Censorship
The power of the printed word is most often seen in the way governments seek to regulate and suppress print. The colonial government kept continuous track of all books and newspapers published in India and passed numerous laws to control the press.

During the First World War, under the Defence of India Rules, 22 newspapers had to furnish securities. Of these, 18 shut down rather than comply with government orders. The Sedition Committee Report under Rowlatt in 1919 further strengthened controls that led to imposition of penalties on various newspapers. At the outbreak of the Second World War, the Defence of India Act was passed, allowing censoring of reports of war-related topics. All reports about the Quit India movement came under its purview. In August 1942, about 90 newspapers were suppressed.

(34.1) Explain the meaning of ‘censor’.
(34.2) Why did the colonial administration keep an eye on books and newspapers ?
(34.3) Why did Gandhiji start a nationwide Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act ? Explain any two reasons.
solution:
(34.1) To censor means to examine and suppress or restrict information, writings or reports considered objectionable by the authorities.
(34.2) The colonial administration monitored books and newspapers to control the press and prevent the spread of ideas critical of British rule.
(34.3) Gandhiji opposed the Rowlatt Act because it curtailed civil liberties and allowed detention without trial. He considered it unjust and a threat to basic rights.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the given source and answer the questions that follow :

An Experiment in Brazil
A city called Porto Alegre in Brazil has carried out an extraordinary experiment in combining decentralisation with participative democracy. The city has set up a parallel organisation operating alongside the municipal council, enabling local inhabitants to take real decisions for their city. The nearly 13 lakh people in this city get to participate in making the budget for their own city. The city is divided into many sectors or what we call wards. Each sector has a meeting, like that of the gram sabha, in which anyone living in that area can participate. There are some meetings to discuss issues that affect the entire city. Any citizen of the city can participate in those meetings. The budget of the city is discussed in these meetings. The proposals are put to the municipality that takes a final decision about it.

(35.1) Explain the meaning of participatory democracy.
(35.2) In the context of separation of powers, the given example defines which type of government ?
(35.3) Describe the structure of the system in India which is almost similar to the above example of Brazil.
solution:
(35.1) Participatory democracy is a system in which citizens directly participate in decision-making and governance.
(35.2) It describes a decentralised form of government in which power is shared with local bodies and citizens.
(35.3) India has a three-tier system of local self-government: Gram Panchayats at village level, Municipalities at urban level and higher local bodies within the constitutional framework of decentralisation.

subject: Social Science
question:

Loans From Cooperatives
Besides banks, the other major source of cheap credit in rural areas are the cooperative societies (or cooperatives). Members of a cooperative pool their resources for cooperation in certain areas. There are several types of cooperatives possible such as farmers cooperatives, weavers cooperatives, industrial workers cooperatives, etc. Krishak Cooperative functions in a village not very far away from Sonpur. It has 2300 farmers as members. It accepts deposits from its members. With these deposits as collateral, the Cooperative has obtained a large loan from the bank. These funds are used to provide loans to members. Once these loans are repaid, another round of lending can take place.

Krishak Cooperative provides loans for the purchase of agricultural implements, loans for cultivation and agricultural trade, fishery loans, loans for construction of houses and for a variety of other expenses.

(36.1) Cooperative societies come under which source of credit ?
(36.2) Mention any two sources of capital of cooperative societies.
(36.3) Explain the role of cooperative societies in increasing the income of farmers.
solution:
(36.1) Cooperative societies are a formal source of credit.
(36.2) Two sources are members’ deposits/savings and loans obtained from banks.
(36.3) Cooperatives provide affordable loans for agricultural inputs, cultivation and trade, helping farmers invest in productive activities and increase their income.

Statement I : Information and communication technology stimulate the process of globalisation.
Statement II : It is used to contact each other, receive information instantly and communicate with remote areas.
Options :
(A) Both statements I and II are correct and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
(B) Both statements I and II are correct, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
(C) Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
(D) Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct.
solution: (A) Both statements I and II are correct and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.

subject: Social Science
question: “Globalisation is the process of rapid integration and interconnection between countries.” Explain the statement with examples.
solution: Globalisation connects countries through trade, investment, technology, production and movement of goods and services. For example, multinational companies produce and sell goods across different countries.

subject: Social Science
question: Explain the role of planning for judicious use of resources.
solution: Resource planning helps identify and inventory resources, develop suitable technologies and institutions, and match resource development with overall national development so that resources are used carefully and sustainably.

subject: Social Science
question: “The Constitution of India provides to all citizens the freedom to profess any religion.” Support the statement by giving two arguments.
solution: Every citizen has the freedom to profess, practice and propagate any religion. The Constitution also prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion and guarantees equality before law.

subject: Social Science
question:
(a) How did reinterpretation of history become a means of creating a sense of nationalism by the end of the 19th century in India ? Explain.
OR
(b) How did symbols and icons contribute to create a feeling of nationalism among the people in the national movement of India ? Explain.
solution:
(a) Nationalist writers highlighted India’s glorious past, achievements and cultural heritage to create pride and a shared national identity.
OR
(b) Symbols and icons such as Bharat Mata, the tricolour flag and national songs created a sense of unity and helped people identify with the nation.

subject: Social Science
question: Analyse the role of women in the ‘Civil Disobedience Movement’.
solution: Women participated in large numbers in protests, picketing of liquor and foreign cloth shops, and civil disobedience activities. Many were arrested, and their participation broadened the mass base of the national movement.

subject: Social Science
concept: Functions and challenges of political parties
question:
(a) Describe three main functions of political parties.
OR
(b) Describe three major challenges faced by the political parties in India.
solution:
(a) Political parties contest elections, form and run governments, and shape public opinion and policies.
OR
(b) Major challenges include lack of internal democracy, dynastic succession, money and muscle power, and limited meaningful choices for voters.

subject: Social Science
question: Explain the vertical distribution of power given in the Indian Constitution.
solution: Power is divided among different levels of government: Union, State and Local governments. Each level has its own jurisdiction and powers, with constitutional provisions defining their responsibilities.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the story of Rinjha and answer the question that follows :
Story of Rinjha
Rinjha lived with her family in a small village at the outskirts of Diphu in Assam. She enjoys watching her family members clearing, slashing and burning a patch of land for cultivation. She often helps them in irrigating the fields with water running through a bamboo canal from the nearby spring. She loves the surroundings and wants to stay here as long as she can, but this little girl has no idea about the declining fertility of the soil and her family’s search for a fresh patch of land in the next season.
Suggest any three measures to Rinjha so that the fertility of the soil of her fields remains intact for a long time.
solution: She should practise crop rotation, use organic manure and compost, and adopt soil conservation measures such as contour ploughing and controlled use of fertilisers.

subject: Social Science
question: Explain the role of primary sector in employment generation in India.
solution: The primary sector provides employment to a large part of India’s population, especially in rural areas. Agriculture, animal husbandry, fishing, forestry and mining directly and indirectly support livelihoods.

subject: Social Science
chapter: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
concept: Balkan region and First World War
question:
(a) How did tension in the Balkan region lead to the First World War ? Explain.
OR
(b) How was the ‘British Nation’ created ? Explain.
solution:
(a) Balkan nationalism and rivalry among European powers created intense conflict. The Ottoman Empire’s decline, competing national claims and alliances increased tensions, and the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand triggered the First World War.
OR
(b) The British nation was formed through a long process of union. The Act of Union 1707 united England and Scotland, while Ireland was incorporated through the Act of Union 1801. English culture, symbols and institutions were promoted to build a British identity.

subject: Social Science
question:
(a) Explain the importance of manufacturing industry in the Indian economy.
OR
(b) Explain the inter-relationship between agriculture and industry.
solution:
(a) Manufacturing adds value to raw materials, creates employment, supports other sectors, earns foreign exchange and promotes economic development.
OR
(b) Agriculture supplies raw materials to industries, while industries provide agricultural machinery, fertilisers, pesticides, irrigation equipment and markets for farm products.

subject: Social Science
question:
(a) How is income an important factor in assessing the development of a country ? Mention the classification done by the World Bank.
OR
(b) How has the overuse of underground water created a serious crisis in many parts of India ? Explain with examples in the context of sustainable development.
solution:
(a) Income indicates the average material standard of living. The World Bank classifies countries mainly on the basis of per capita income into low-income and higher-income groups, with income thresholds used for classification.
OR
(b) Excessive groundwater extraction lowers water tables and creates scarcity. It can lead to falling water levels, declining agricultural productivity and water stress. Sustainable development requires conservation, rainwater harvesting and controlled extraction.

subject: Social Science
question:
(a) How is democracy better than other types of government ? Analyse.
OR
(b) Analyse the role of democracy in reducing inequality and poverty.
solution:
(a) Democracy provides accountable and responsive government, improves the quality of decision-making, provides peaceful ways to resolve differences, enhances dignity and allows correction of mistakes through elections.
OR
(b) Democracy gives equal political rights and opportunities to citizens and allows disadvantaged groups to raise their demands. However, political equality does not automatically remove economic inequality and poverty.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the given source and answer the questions that follow :
Arun’s Story
Arun supervises the work of one farm labourer. Arun has seven acres of land. He is one of the few persons in Sonpur to receive bank loan for cultivation. The interest rate on the loan is 8·5 per cent per annum, and can be repaid anytime in the next three years. Arun plans to repay the loan after harvest by selling a part of the crop. He then intends to store the rest of the potatoes in a cold storage and apply for a fresh loan from the bank against the cold storage receipt. The bank offers this facility to farmers who have taken crop loan from them.
(34.1) Under which source does Arun’s loan come ?
(34.2) Mention one important term of credit for taking a loan from the bank.
(34.3) How is Arun’s loan beneficial ? Explain any two reasons.
solution:
(34.1) Arun’s loan comes under the formal source of credit.
(34.2) Interest rate is an important term of credit.
(34.3) The loan is beneficial because it is available at a relatively low interest rate and allows repayment within a flexible period. The cold-storage receipt can also help him obtain another loan.

subject: Social Science
chapter: Print Culture and the Modern World
concept: Print Culture and the French Revolution
question:
Read the given source and answer the questions that follow :
Print Culture and the French Revolution
Many historians have argued that print culture created the conditions within which French Revolution occurred.
Some arguments have been usually put forward in this context.
First : print popularised the ideas of the Enlightenment thinkers. Collectively, their writings provided a critical commentary on tradition, superstition and despotism. They argued for the rule of reason rather than custom, and demanded that everything be judged through the application of reason and rationality. They attacked the sacred authority of the Church and the despotic power of the state, thus eroding the legitimacy of a social order based on tradition. The writings of Voltaire and Rousseau were read widely; and those who read these books saw the world through new eyes, eyes that were questioning, critical and rational.
Second : print created a new culture of dialogue and debate. All values, norms and institutions were re-evaluated and discussed by a public that had become aware of the power of reason, and recognised the need to question existing ideas and beliefs. Within this public culture, new ideas of social revolution came into being.
(35.1) What impact did the ideas of Enlightenment thinkers have on society ?
(35.2) How did print culture affect religion in France ?
(35.3) How did print culture contribute to the social revolution in France ?
solution:
(35.1) Enlightenment ideas encouraged people to question tradition, superstition and despotism and promoted reason and rational thinking.
(35.2) Print criticised the authority of the Church and encouraged people to question religious beliefs and institutions.
(35.3) Print created a culture of debate in which existing values and institutions were questioned, helping spread new ideas of social and political change.

subject: Social Science
question:
Read the given source and answer the questions that follow :
Decentralisation in India
The need for decentralisation was recognised in our Constitution. Since then, there have been several attempts to decentralise power to the level of villages and towns. Panchayats in villages and municipalities in urban areas were set up in all the States. But these were directly under the control of state governments. Elections to these local governments were not held regularly. Local governments did not have any powers or resources of their own. Thus, there was very little decentralisation in effective terms.
A major step towards decentralisation was taken in 1992. The Constitution was amended to make the third-tier of democracy more powerful and effective.
(36.1) At how many levels has decentralisation of power been done in the Indian Constitution ?
(36.2) Explain the role of local self-government in solving problems.
(36.3) “Local government is the best way to realise one important principle of democracy, namely local self-government.” Explain the statement.
solution:
(36.1) Decentralisation of power has been done at three levels: Union, State and Local.
(36.2) Local self-government allows local people to participate in decision-making and solve local problems according to local needs.
(36.3) Local government brings decision-making closer to the people, increases participation and accountability, and enables citizens to manage issues affecting their daily lives.

subject: Social Science
question: Assume there are four families in a locality. If the incomes of these four families in a week are ₹ 2,000, ₹ 5,000, ₹ 3,000 and ₹ 6,000, then the weekly average income of the locality will be – (A) ₹ 4,000 (B) ₹ 5,000 (C) ₹ 2,000 (D) ₹ 1,000
solution: Average income = (2000 + 5000 + 3000 + 6000) / 4 = ₹4000. Correct option: (A).

solution: Literacy rate is measured for the population aged 7 years and above. Correct option: (B).

solution: Odia is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution. Correct option: (D).

subject: Social Science

solution: Democracy is based on the rule of people with freedom. Correct option: (C).

subject: Social Science
question: Two statements are given below. They are Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Read both the statements and choose the correct option. (D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
solution: Both the Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason explains the Assertion. Correct option: (A).

subject: Social Science
question: How is horizontal power sharing different from vertical ? Explain.
solution: Horizontal power sharing is among different organs of government at the same level, such as the legislature, executive and judiciary. Vertical power sharing is among different levels of government, such as Union, State and Local governments.

subject: Social Science
chapter: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
question: “Conservative regimes set up in Europe in 1815 were autocratic.” Support the statement by giving any two arguments.
solution: The conservative regimes opposed liberal and democratic ideas. They did not tolerate criticism and imposed restrictions on freedom of speech, press and political activities.

subject: Social Science
question: (a) Differentiate between Intensive Subsistence and Plantation Farming. OR (b) Differentiate between Kharif and Zaid cropping seasons.
solution: (a) Intensive subsistence farming is practised on small plots with high labour input and is mainly for subsistence. Plantation farming is large-scale commercial farming of a single crop such as tea, coffee or rubber. OR (b) Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon and harvested in autumn, such as rice and maize. Zaid crops are grown between the Rabi and Kharif seasons, such as watermelon and cucumber.

subject: Social Science
question: ‘Different people have different notions of development.’ Explain the statement with examples.
solution: Different people have different needs and priorities. For example, a landless rural labourer may want more days of employment and better wages, while a prosperous farmer may want better irrigation facilities and higher crop prices.

subject: Social Science
chapter: The Making of a Global World
question: (a) How was the ‘Silk Route’ an example of vibrant pre-modern trade ? Explain. OR (b) How did food promote long-distance cultural contacts in the pre-modern world ? Explain.
solution: (a) The Silk Routes connected Asia with Europe and North Africa. Traders carried silk, spices, textiles and other goods across long distances. Along with goods, ideas, religions and cultural practices also travelled. OR (b) Food such as noodles, pasta, potatoes, maize and other crops travelled across regions and continents. New foods changed diets and connected different cultures through trade and migration.

subject: Social Science
question: ‘Manufacturing sector is considered the backbone of an economic development.’ Justify the statement.
solution: Manufacturing adds value to raw materials, creates employment, reduces dependence on agricultural income, promotes trade and earns foreign exchange. It also supports the growth of other sectors by creating demand for raw materials, transport and services.

subject: Social Science
question: “Tertiary sector has a pivotal role in the economy of the country.” Support your answer with day-to-day examples.
solution: The tertiary sector provides services required by people and other sectors. Examples include transport, banking, communication, education, healthcare, trade and insurance. These services support agriculture and manufacturing and improve economic activity.

subject: Social Science
question: Explain any three responsibilities carried out by the political parties in a democracy.
solution: Political parties contest elections, formulate policies and programmes, make laws through elected representatives, form and run governments, and act as a link between citizens and the government.

subject: Social Science
question: Give any three suggestions to increase the employment in rural society and explain them.
solution: Employment can be increased by improving irrigation facilities, promoting small-scale and agro-based industries, and expanding education, healthcare, transport and other services. These activities create additional employment opportunities in rural areas.

subject: Social Science
question: “The Gandhian idea of Satyagraha, emphasized the power of truth and struggle against injustice.” Explain the statement with examples. OR How did people belonging to different communities, regions and language groups develop a sense of collective belonging in the late-nineteenth century India ? Explain with examples.
solution: Satyagraha was based on truth, non-violence and peaceful resistance against injustice. Gandhi used it in Champaran, Kheda and Ahmedabad and later in the Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience Movements. OR A sense of collective belonging developed through the idea of Bharat Mata, folklore, songs, reinterpretation of history, national symbols and participation in mass movements. These created a shared feeling of belonging to one nation.

subject: Social Science
question: (a) How is energy a basic requirement for economic development ? Explain with examples. OR (b) How do minerals occur ? Explain with examples.
solution: (a) Energy is required for agriculture, industries, transport, communication and domestic activities. Coal, petroleum, natural gas, electricity and renewable sources provide energy for economic activities. OR (b) Minerals occur in veins and lodes in igneous and metamorphic rocks, in beds or layers in sedimentary rocks, as alluvial deposits and as oceanic deposits. Examples include metallic minerals in veins and coal in sedimentary layers.

subject: Social Science
question: (a) How are democratic governments accountable, responsible and legitimate ? Explain. OR (b) How does democracy promote social justice and equality ? Explain.
solution: (a) Democratic governments are accountable because citizens can question and replace them through elections. They are responsible because they respond to people's needs and follow constitutional rules. They are legitimate because they are elected by the people. OR (b) Democracy promotes equality by giving equal political rights, universal adult franchise and equal opportunity to participate in government. It also provides mechanisms to address discrimination and social inequalities.

subject: Social Science
question: (a) “Rapid improvement in technology has been one major factor that has stimulated the globalisation process.” Explain the statement with examples. OR (b) “Foreign trade and foreign investment policies are the aspects of liberalisation and globalisation.” Explain the statement with examples.
solution: (a) Improvements in information and communication technology, transport and production have made it easier to move goods, services, information and capital across countries. Internet, mobile communication, faster transport and modern production systems have accelerated globalisation. OR (b) Liberalisation removed many restrictions on foreign trade and investment. This enabled MNCs to invest in India, expand production, establish partnerships and connect Indian producers with international markets.

subject: Social Science
question: Read the following extract and answer the questions that follow: How many languages do we have in India? The answer depends on how one counts it. The latest information that we have is from the Census of India held in 2011. This census recorded more than 1300 distinct languages which people mentioned as their mother tongues. These languages were grouped together under some major languages. For example, languages like Bhojpuri, Magadhi, Bundelkhandi, Chhattisgarhi, Rajasthani and many others were grouped together under ‘Hindi’. Even after this grouping, the Census found 121 major languages. Of these, 22 languages are now included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution and are therefore called ‘Scheduled Languages’. Others are called ‘Non-Scheduled Languages’. In terms of languages, India is perhaps the most diverse country in the world. (34.1) How many languages were recorded as mother tongues in the 2011 Census of India ? (34.2) How were the languages grouped together in the Census report ? (34.3) How does the inclusion of languages in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution contribute to linguistic diversity ? Explain.
solution: (34.1) More than 1300 distinct languages were recorded as mother tongues. (34.2) The languages were grouped together under major languages. (34.3) The Eighth Schedule recognises 22 major languages as Scheduled Languages, giving them constitutional recognition while other languages continue as Non-Scheduled Languages. subject: Social Science
chapter: Print Culture and the Modern World
question: Read the following source and answer the questions that follow: The power of the printed word is most often seen in the way governments seek to regulate and suppress print. The colonial government kept continuous track of all books and newspapers published in India and passed numerous laws to control the press. During the First World War, under the Defense of India Rules, 22 newspapers had to furnish securities. Of these, 18 shut down rather than comply with government orders. The Sedition Committee Report under Rowlatt in 1919 further strengthened controls that led to imposition of penalties on various newspapers. At the outbreak of the Second World War, the Defense of India Act was passed, allowing censoring of reports of war-related topics. All reports about the Quit India Movement came under its purview. In August 1942, about 90 newspapers were suppressed. (35.1) What method did the colonial government employ to keep track of Indian newspapers ? (35.2) How did the colonial government’s laws affect the press ? (35.3) Analyse the impact of ‘Sedition Committee’ on Newspapers.
solution: (35.1) The colonial government continuously monitored books and newspapers published in India. (35.2) The laws imposed restrictions, censorship, penalties and security requirements on newspapers, forcing some newspapers to shut down. (35.3) The Sedition Committee Report of 1919 strengthened government control over the press. It led to penalties and restrictions on newspapers and reduced their freedom to publish material critical of the colonial government.

subject: Social Science
question: Read the following source and answer the questions that follow: Project Tiger, one of the well publicised wildlife campaigns in the world, was launched in 1973. Tiger conservation has been viewed not only as an effort to save an endangered species but with equal importance as a means of preserving biotypes of sizeable magnitude. Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand, Sunderbans National Park in West Bengal, Bandhavgarh National Park in Madhya Pradesh, Sariska Wildlife Sanctuary in Rajasthan, Manas Tiger Reserve in Assam and Periyar Tiger Reserve in Kerala are some examples of the tiger reserves in India. (36.1) Why was ‘Project Tiger’ considered a significant step for Tiger Conservation ? (36.2) What role did India play in the global tiger population ? (36.3) Mention any two major threats to the wildlife species.
solution: (36.1) Project Tiger was significant because it aimed to protect the endangered tiger and preserve large ecosystems and biodiversity. (36.2) India and Nepal provided habitat to about two-thirds of the surviving tiger population of the world, making India an important country for tiger conservation. (36.3) Major threats include poaching for trade, shrinking habitat, depletion of prey species and increasing human population. Any two are acceptable.

solution: Valli's desire is personal: she wants to ride a bus and experience the outside world independently. Through planning, saving money and courage, she fulfils this desire. Mandela's vision is broader: he wants freedom and equality for all South Africans. Through struggle, sacrifice and perseverance, he helps establish a democratic South Africa.

subject: English
chapter: The Ball Poem and The Sermon at Benares
question: Prepare a speech on “How to Deal with Loss — Personal or Material” with reference to the commonality of themes in ‘The Ball Poem’ and ‘The Sermon at Benares’.
solution: Both texts teach that loss is an unavoidable part of life. The boy in The Ball Poem learns to accept material loss, while Kisa Gotami learns through Buddha that death and separation are universal. We should accept loss, learn from it and continue life with understanding and courage.

subject: English
question: Imagine that Griffin's conscience pricks him and he decides to write a diary entry about misusing science and endangering society.
solution: Griffin would express regret for using his scientific discovery selfishly. He would acknowledge that invisibility gave him power but he used it for theft, violence and causing fear. He would realise that scientific knowledge must be guided by morality and responsibility. He would resolve to use his intelligence for the welfare of society rather than personal gain.

subject: English
question: Trace the character arc of Matilda in Guy de Maupassant's ‘The Necklace’.
solution: Matilda begins as a dissatisfied woman who dreams of wealth and luxury. Her desire to appear rich leads her to borrow a necklace and later lose it. She and her husband spend ten years repaying the cost of the replacement. Hardship transforms her into a hardworking and responsible woman. At the end, she learns that the original necklace was only an imitation, revealing the tragic consequence of her vanity.

subject: English
question:
Which of the following statements best describes the difference between renewable energy sources and alternate energy sources?
(A) Alternative energy sources are more expensive than renewable energy sources.
(B) Renewable energy sources are inexhaustible whereas alternate energy sources could be exhaustible.
(C) Alternative energy sources are as renewable as renewable energy sources.
(D) Renewable energy sources are exhaustible but alternative energy sources are inexhaustible.
solution: (B) Renewable energy sources are inexhaustible whereas alternate energy sources could be exhaustible.

subject: English
question:
What is the tone of the writer in the given lines from para (4)? Rationalise your response in about 40 words.
“However, thanks to increased demand, more experienced energy developers, competitive supply chains, improved renewable technologies, and enhanced energy efficiency capabilities, that’s no longer the case”.
solution: The tone is optimistic and encouraging. The writer highlights improvements in demand, technology, supply chains and energy efficiency to show that alternative energy is now more practical and accessible.

subject: English
question:
Complete the sentence appropriately:
In the past, alternative energy sources were not used much by the consumers because ________.
solution: the equipment necessary to harness energy from alternative sources used to be so expensive that it wasn’t practical for consumer use.

subject: English
question:
The passage includes some words that are opposites of each other. From the sets (a) to (e) below, identify two sets of antonyms:
(a) generate and produce
(b) exhaustible and inexhaustible
(c) subtle and versatile
(d) power and energy
(e) sustainable and exhaustible
solution: (b) exhaustible and inexhaustible; (e) sustainable and exhaustible.

subject: English
question: Who is the leader of renewable energy pack and why?
solution: Wind energy is the leader of the renewable energy pack because it is the most energy-efficient renewable source mentioned in the passage.

subject: English
question: Based on the reading of the passage, examine, in about 40 words, the difference between geothermal electricity and hydroelectricity.
solution: Geothermal electricity is generated by tapping underground reservoirs of hot water and steam, while hydroelectricity is generated from moving water when water behind a dam causes turbine blades to move and produce electricity.

subject: English
question:
What is the message conveyed by the passage?
(A) Only those energy sources should be used which are renewable.
(B) Wind energy is a renewable as well as inexhaustible source of energy.
(C) There are plenty of renewable energy sources that can be used to replace traditional energy sources.
(D) Alternative energy sources are the emerging energy trends and are still evolving.
solution: (C) There are plenty of renewable energy sources that can be used to replace traditional energy sources.

question:

Hydroelectricity as a renewable energy source is used for residential as well as commercial purposes.
solution: True.

question: The bursting of the sewage pipe in your colony has led to an overflow of sewage making it impossible to travel on A2 and A3 streets of your colony. solution: Write a formal letter to the local MLA describing the sewage overflow, unbearable stench, traffic jams and mosquito breeding, and request immediate action to repair the sewage pipe and resolve the problem.

Write a letter to the Director, Outdoor Adventures mentioning your proposed travel dates, number of students and teacher escorts. Find out about the mode of travel options, boarding, lodging, trekking gear, camping facilities and cost.
solution: Write a formal enquiry letter to the Director, Outdoor Adventures mentioning the proposed travel dates, number of students and teacher escorts, and asking about travel, boarding, lodging, trekking gear, camping facilities and cost.

subject: English
question:
The data given below represents the percentage of some of the electronic devices used in India. Summarize and analyse the data in about 120 words. Give all necessary details and compare the segments where relevant.
Television — 86%
Electronic toys — 40%
Mobile phones — 96%
Laptops — 38%
Refrigerators — 69%
Kitchen appliances — 84%
solution: The data shows that mobile phones have the highest usage at 96%, followed by television at 86% and kitchen appliances at 84%. Refrigerators are used by 69%, while electronic toys and laptops have lower usage at 40% and 38% respectively. Thus, communication and household devices are more widely used than laptops and electronic toys.

subject: English
question:
Based on the following extract, write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words:
“One of the biggest changes in our lives over the past decade is the ability to order items online and have them delivered to our doorstep. The prevalence of this raises an important question of how it affects our environment. Though buyers conserve fuel and reduce emissions from their vehicles, it is replaced by additional mileage of truck routes. Also a large amount of wastage is generated from packaging such as cardboard boxes, bubble wraps, plastic bags etc.”
You may begin like this:
As a responsible citizen, I believe .....
You may end like this:
For these reasons, I believe, we need to limit the wastage associated with online shopping.
solution: Online shopping provides convenience and may reduce individual vehicle trips, but delivery vehicles add mileage and packaging creates cardboard, bubble-wrap and plastic waste. Responsible consumers and companies should reduce unnecessary packaging, use recyclable materials and adopt efficient delivery practices to limit environmental damage.

subject: English
chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
question:
What do you infer from the following statement?
“The inauguration would be the largest gathering ever of international leaders on South African Soil.”
solution: It shows the historic importance of the inauguration and the international recognition of South Africa’s transition to a democratic, non-racial government.

subject: English
chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
question: Explain in about 40 words the effective shift from white supremacy to a rainbow gathering.
solution: The Union Buildings had once been a seat of white supremacy. They now became the site of a gathering of different colours and nations for the installation of South Africa’s first democratic non-racial government, symbolising equality and unity.

State any one inference about Anne from the given context.
“Anyone could ramble on and leave big spaces between the words, but the trick was to come up with convincing arguments to prove the necessity of talking.”
solution: Anne is intelligent, witty and confident enough to defend her talkative nature with convincing arguments.

subject: English
chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
question: In about 40 words, elaborate on the justification Anne gives for her talkative nature.
solution: Anne says that talking is a student’s trait and that she will try to keep it under control. However, she believes she cannot completely cure herself because her mother is equally talkative and it is an inherited trait.

(B) persuasive
(C) nostalgic

solution: (B) persuasive

solution: talk continuously / talk at length without focus

subject: English
question: Explain the contrast created by the words, ‘stalks’ and ‘few steps of his cage’.
solution: ‘Stalks’ suggests the tiger’s natural, powerful movement, whereas ‘few steps of his cage’ shows the restriction of his freedom and movement in captivity.

subject: English
question:
Which of the following best describes the tiger’s feelings in the context?
(A) anger
(B) conflicted
(C) pessimism
(D) apprehension
solution: (A) anger

subject: English
question: Comment in about 40 words on the poet’s use of imagery in the above extract.
solution: The poet uses vivid imagery such as ‘vivid stripes’, ‘pads of velvet quiet’ and ‘quiet rage’. These images present the tiger’s graceful natural beauty while highlighting his silent anger and confinement.

subject: English
question: Which word in the stanza means the same as ‘clear and bright’?
solution: vivid

subject: English
question: When the poet says that “no one buys a ball back”, what does he refer to in the context of the poem?
solution: He means that the emotional value and memories associated with the lost ball cannot be brought back by simply buying another ball.

subject: English
question:
Complete the sentence with an appropriate option:
The lines from the poem tell us that the boy is experiencing ______.
(A) distress
(B) terror
(C) realisation
(D) elation
solution: (C) realisation

subject: English
question: What is the significance of the term “desperate” used to describe the boy’s eyes in the poem, and how does it contribute to the overall mood and tone of the poem?
solution: ‘Desperate’ reflects the boy’s intense pain and helplessness after the loss. It contributes to the sorrowful and serious mood and shows his struggle to understand and accept loss.

subject: English
question: Identify and discuss the poet’s use of metaphor in the poem “The Ball Poem”.
solution: The ball is a metaphor for the boy’s childhood, memories and emotional attachment. Its loss represents his first important experience of loss and learning to accept it.

subject: English
question: Explain the irony in the chapter, “A Letter to God”.
solution: Lencho has complete faith in God but suspects the post office employees of stealing part of the money sent to him. The irony is that the employees actually collected and sent the money to help him.

subject: English
question: “During our childhood in Goa, the baker used to be our friend, companion and guide.” What does this statement imply in relation to the character of the baker?
solution: The baker was a familiar and important part of village life. He visited homes regularly, interacted with children and supplied bread, becoming a friendly companion and guide in the narrator’s childhood.

subject: English
question: It is our attitude towards a situation that makes it positive or negative. Do you agree with it? Express your views with reference to the poem ‘Dust of Snow’.
solution: Yes. The poet’s gloomy mood changes after a simple natural incident in which snow falls from a hemlock tree. The experience refreshes him and saves part of his day, showing that attitude can change the way we experience a situation.

subject: English
chapter: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
question: Belinda and other animals have been described as brave. But on seeing the pirate they behaved in a cowardly way. How did they react? (A Tale of Custard, The Dragon)
solution: Belinda cried for help, Ink ran away, Blink hid and Mustard fled. They were frightened by the pirate and failed to show the bravery they had claimed. Custard alone faced the pirate and defeated him.

subject: English
question: Flying is a natural act in birds. Then why was the young seagull ‘exhausted by the strange exercise’? Justify the given statement with reference to baby seagull’s fear. (His First Flight)
solution: The young seagull had never flown before and was afraid to leave the ledge. His fear made his first attempt stressful and exhausting. Once he overcame the fear, he discovered that flying was natural for him.

subject: English
question: Do you think Bholi could have confidently refused to marry Bishamber if she wasn’t educated? Give reasons. (Bholi)
solution: No. Education and her teacher’s support gave Bholi confidence, self-respect and the ability to speak for herself. Without education, she might have remained timid and accepted the marriage despite Bishamber’s demand for dowry.

subject: English
question: Who was Henry? What role did he play in Ausable’s plan? (The Midnight Visitor)
solution: Henry was the waiter at the hotel. His expected arrival helped Ausable make Max believe the false story about a balcony. When Henry knocked, Max tried to escape through the window and fell into Ausable’s trap.

subject: English
question: Horace Danby was a typical thief. Describe how he planned his work. (A Question of Trust)
solution: Horace carefully selected houses, studied their owners’ routines and waited for suitable opportunities. He carried tools, used gloves to avoid fingerprints and planned his robberies methodically.

subject: English
question:
Valli was sensitive, but at the same time, she was fearless and quite determined. Think of another character from your text book, who displayed similar character traits. Compare and contrast the lives of Valli and the other character, that you have chosen from the text of Two Stories about Flying.
You may begin this way.
The characters who are fearless and determined from two texts are Valli and ________.
(Reference : Madam Rides a Bus & Two Stories about Flying)
solution: The characters who are fearless and determined are Valli and the young seagull. Valli plans carefully and courageously fulfils her wish to ride a bus alone. The young seagull initially fears flying but overcomes his fear when hunger forces him to fly. Valli’s courage comes from planning and confidence, while the seagull’s develops through necessity. Both become more confident through experience.

subject: English
chapter: The Proposal and From the Diary of Anne Frank
question:
Based on your understanding of the Play ‘The Proposal’, what do you think of relationships? Prepare a speech draft on relationships based on Natalya’s and Anne Frank’s characters.
You may begin this way.
Good morning everyone.
Relationships are the bond between two people based on mutual likes, understanding, need or love. I’d like to discuss relationships as portrayed in the two texts ……
You may end this way
To conclude, I’d like to say that …… .
Thank you,
(Reference : The Proposal & from the Diary of Anne Frank)
solution: Relationships need understanding, trust and communication. Natalya’s relationship in The Proposal is humorous and argumentative, while Anne Frank values genuine friendship and emotional connection. The two texts show that relationships can be affected by conflict and personal interests, but mutual respect, openness and understanding make them meaningful.

subject: English
question: Griffin’s brilliance as a man of science fades before his darker traits. Give reasons from the text to support your answer. (Footprints Without Feet)
solution: Griffin is scientifically brilliant because he discovers how to make the human body invisible. However, he misuses his discovery for theft, revenge, violence and selfish gain. He burns a landlord’s house, steals clothes and money, frightens people and attacks others. His scientific brilliance is therefore overshadowed by his immoral and irresponsible behaviour.

subject: English
question: Hari Singh says — “He knew it but neither his lips nor his eyes showed anything.” Anil successfully addressed the situation by not addressing it all. Elaborate based on your reading of ‘The Thief’s Story’.
solution: Anil understood that Hari had stolen the money but deliberately avoided confronting him. His silence and trust gave Hari a chance to feel ashamed and change. Instead of punishing him, Anil continued to treat him kindly, encouraging Hari to return the money and choose an honest life.

subject: English

subject: English

solution: The passage states that adulterants such as beetroot, pomegranate, silk fibres, oil and wax are added, while powdered saffron may be mixed with turmeric and paprika.

subject: English

solution: It shows that silk is valued for its natural softness, smooth texture and comfort. It can also absorb and release moisture, helping regulate body temperature and keeping the wearer cool and dry.
